name: Carnivore diet

lead: The carnivore diet limits food to animal products such as meat, eggs and dairy, excluding fruit, vegetables and grains. Its modern popularity dates from around 2018, and in looksmaxxing communities people follow it for leanness, clearer skin and better body composition, with some crediting it for a sharper jaw.

Proponents say removing plant foods removes irritants and processed foods, and raises protein and fat intake, which they link to less bloat, leanness, hormone levels and skin. A 2026 scoping review found nine human studies, noting reported weight loss, increased satiety and improvements in some inflammatory or metabolic markers, with evidence quality described as very limited. No studies of skin or facial structure were found.

paras: People eat mainly beef, eggs, fish and dairy, with stricter versions limited to beef, salt and water, and often follow it for weeks to months while tracking weight and skin.

Reviews report potential shortfalls of vitamins C and D, calcium, magnesium, iodine and fiber, and higher LDL and total cholesterol. Dietetic bodies including the British Dietetic Association and Dietitians Australia reject the diet, and high red meat intake is linked to higher risks of colon cancer and gout.

angle.text: Eating only animal foods is meant to cut bloat and inflammation, lean out the body and face and clear the skin. Followers credit it with these results; a 2026 review located nine small human studies, none on skin or facial appearance.

lead: The carnivore diet is an almost exclusively animal-based dietary pattern, permitting meat, eggs and dairy and eliminating plant foods. [1][2] Wikipedia notes antecedents in nineteenth-century meat-and-water regimens and dates modern promotion to around 2018, when surgeon-turned-advocate Shawn Baker published a book on it; a stricter beef, salt and water version called the lion diet later spread on TikTok. [3]
In looksmaxxing communities it is discussed as a route to skin, leanness, body composition and jaw or bone-related claims, with other members arguing against it. [4][5][6]

A 2026 scoping review identified nine human studies, noting reported weight loss, increased satiety and improvements in some inflammatory or metabolic markers, alongside risks of nutrient deficiencies and elevated cholesterol, with evidence quality described as very limited. [1] Wikipedia reports that nutrition scientists and dietetic bodies generally reject it. [3]
infobox: Meat, eggs, dairy; strictest form beef, salt, water [3]

paras: Carnivore eating is described in the literature as a newly popular, sparsely studied form of ketogenic diet in which plant foods are removed so that nearly all nutrition comes from animal-sourced foods. [2] No standardized definition exists. [1]

Wikipedia traces the idea to the 1800s, including a regimen promoted by physician James H. Salisbury, and says Jordan Peterson and his daughter Mikhaila were prominent adherents of the lion diet. [3] A 2021 survey of 2,029 self-identified carnivore dieters recruited through social media described their practices and self-reported health. [7]

A 2026 scoping review of nine human studies reported individual findings of weight reduction, increased satiety and potential improvements in inflammatory or metabolic markers, along with potential nutrient deficiencies and elevated LDL and total cholesterol, and one case of deteriorating health. The authors judged the evidence very limited because of small samples, short durations and absent control groups. [1]

A 2024 case series of ten patients described a carnivore-ketogenic diet in inflammatory bowel disease. [8] A 2024 modelling study assessed micronutrient adequacy of four carnivore diet versions against national reference values. [9] No studies found examining the diet's effect on skin, jaw structure or facial appearance.

A 2020 review discussed whether plant-free diets can supply all essential nutrients, noting that ketogenic metabolism may change nutrient needs and that evidence is conflicting. [2] The 2026 scoping review lists vitamins C and D, calcium, magnesium, iodine and fiber as potential shortfalls. [1]

A 2025 systematic review argues that meat consumption supports short-term hypertrophy but may be linked to longevity-related harms through pathways including mTOR and IGF-1 activation. [10] Wikipedia lists constipation, raised LDL cholesterol, colon cancer and gout risk, and possible kidney effects as reported concerns. [3]

Looksmax.org threads include members crediting the diet with changes in their game or appearance, members arguing it harms gut health and cardiovascular risk, and a thread framing a choice between it and isotretinoin. [4][5][6]

lore.intro: On looksmax.org the carnivore diet is both promoted as a body and skin strategy and argued against on health grounds. [4][5][6]
